summary: Analysis only. (1) Corrected two statements: I may not call the k = 6 palette-nullity false without a global WeakColoring counterexample - the right wording is that the k = 5 proof does not generalise, since its last step needs the complement of a 3-set to be a 2-set and at k = 6 it has three labels; and the candidate's 0.005 centre ball is a valid sufficient bound, 0.01 being only the sharp threshold for automatic containment. (2) Reconstructed the referee's palette audit: for |x| <= 0.005 every sample circle lies in the annulus, the annulus colouring has finitely many discontinuity rays so circles meet them in finitely many points, and dominated L2 convergence makes every trace limit the exact singleton indicator - so the palette statement is extension-independent there, while ring centres at |x| near 1 see the hole and are not locally determined. (3) Extracted States.two_state_impossible with producer, centre, quantifiers and consumer, plus its k = 6 limitation. (4) The local triangle scenario is proved locally unit-proper (patch radius below 0.005 gives no unit pair; the patch-annulus interface has disjoint label sets; the annulus is properly 3-coloured), and the first global relation that bites is the dual endpoint constraint at ring centres, forcing the patch labels into the palettes at p - e and destroying the outsider mechanism. Necessary, not sufficient.
verified_results: GRADE [P] Correction: the k = 5 palette-nullity proof (palette_triple_null) ends by making the complement of a 3-set a 2-set and invoking the binary step; at k = 6 that complement has three labels, so the mechanism fails. Hence the correct statement is that k = 6 nullity is unproved and this proof does not generalise - not that the statement is false, which would need a global WeakColoring 6 counterexample.

GRADE [P] Correction: the candidate's |x| < 0.005 centre ball is a valid sufficient bound; |x| <= 0.01 is the sharp threshold for every radius-1 circle about x to stay inside 0.99 < |z| < 1.01. Both are legitimate and the difference is immaterial for the local conclusions.

GRADE [C]→[P] The referee's palette verification is accepted and reconstructed from source: IsTrace is a norm limit of sampleCode at centres y_n -> x and radii r_n -> 1; for |x| <= 0.005 all those circles lie in the annulus; the annulus colouring is piecewise constant with nine sector rays plus two circular boundaries, so a circle meets the discontinuity set in finitely many points (an angular null set); the codes therefore converge pointwise off a null set and are dominated by 1, so they converge in L2 to the indicator of the limit colouring. Hence P_x(e) = {c_A(x+e)} a.e., independently of any extension of the colouring off the patch-annulus union.

GRADE [P] The extension-independence is exactly limited to |x| <= 0.005 (or < 0.01): ring centres with |x| near 1 have unit circles that pass through the hole (through x + e = y with |y| < 0.005 when e points toward the origin), so their palettes are determined by the unfilled colouring of the region between patches and annulus.

GRADE [S] States.two_state_impossible (States.lean:243) with RealState (States.lean:92): for measurable c, WeakColoring k c, a centre x, label sets J and K with |univ \(J union K)| <= 2, a measurable Boolean s, RealState x {t | s t = false} J and RealState x {t | s t = true} K, and the 60-degree flip s(t + pi/3) = not(s t) a.e., one derives False. Its consumer is the four-state lemma at States.lean:378 (fourGroup machinery) feeding the exclusion chain, with Lemma 6.7 = step_ban retained downstream. At k = 6 the cardinality hypothesis is harder (two groups must cover four of six labels), so the lemma is weaker at k = 6, not stronger.

GRADE [P] The local triangle scenario is locally unit-proper: a patch of radius rho < 0.005 has diameter below 0.01 so contains no unit pair and any colouring of it is proper; every unit-neighbour of a patch point lies in the annulus and the label sets {0,1,2} and {3,4,5} are disjoint, so all patch-annulus unit pairs are properly coloured; and the annulus is properly 3-coloured by the angular-separation argument. So the local data is consistent and the transition triangles at patch centres genuinely accumulate at 0 for that data.

GRADE [P] The first global relation that bites is the dual endpoint constraint at ring centres: for a patch point p and a unit e, the centre x = p - e lies in the annulus, so the constraint c(p) in P_{p-e}(e) forces the labels {0,1,2} to occur in the palettes at ring centres on the arcs whose circles dip into the patches. That destroys the outsider mechanism the scenario relies on. It is necessary but not sufficient: a palette may hold a patch label and an annulus label simultaneously, so a contradiction needs the unit-scale transport at the same centre, which is precisely what the unfilled region between patches and annulus would determine.
conjectures: The scenario's failure point is structural: at k = 6 the outsider mechanism needs the cycle labels to be absent from every nearby palette, and the dual endpoint constraint denies exactly that at radius 1, because the ring centres see the patches. So any k = 6 accumulation gadget must survive having its cycle labels present in the palettes at radius 1, which is a strictly stronger requirement than the k >= 7 construction faces.

Whether (†) plus the unit-scale transport at ring centres really yields a contradiction is the natural next question; it would need an instance of palette_transport_param at a ring centre with the two-unit decomposition, i.e. global information about the mid-region, not a local centre separation.

States.two_state_impossible is the only single-centre global coupling in the tree that constrains a two-block palette split; at k = 6 it requires the blocks to cover four of six labels plus an alternating Boolean, which the triangle scenario does not provide (its indicator is not alternating), so it does not rule the scenario out.
